You are in charge of fixing one bug in the Python repository checked out at /click (the `click` CLI library; source in /click/src/click/, tests in /click/tests/).

BUG REPORT (from the user): "There is a bug whose fix touches `src/click/_compat.py`, `src/click/_termui_impl.py` and `src/click/utils.py`. Once it is fixed, the test `tests.test_utils::test_echo_no_streams` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

Interpretation: the expected behaviour is that click works when the standard streams are missing, i.e. when `sys.stdout` / `sys.stderr` / `sys.stdin` are `None` (this happens e.g. under `pythonw` on Windows, or when a GUI app has no console). Today `click.echo(...)` calls `_default_text_stdout()` -> `get_text_stdout()` -> `_force_correct_text_writer(sys.stdout, ...)` which crashes with AttributeError/TypeError when `sys.stdout is None`. The likely intended fix (three files):
- `src/click/_compat.py`: make `_make_cached_stream_func` (used for `_default_text_stdin/_stdout/_stderr`) return `None` when the source stream (`sys.stdout` etc.) is `None`, and adjust the type annotations accordingly.
- `src/click/utils.py`: in `echo()`, after resolving `file = _default_text_stderr()/_default_text_stdout()`, return early (do nothing) if the resulting file is `None`.
- `src/click/_termui_impl.py`: in `ProgressBar.__init__`, when `file is None` and `_default_text_stdout()` returns `None`, fall back to `io.StringIO()`; and make `pager()`/`_nullpager` tolerate a `None` stdout (e.g. return early / use a StringIO) so nothing crashes with no streams.

Requirements:
- FIRST run the pre-existing test suite and record the baseline failures: `cd /click && python -m pytest tests -q` (if `click` is not importable, `pip install -e .` first).
- Make the minimal fix. Do NOT edit or delete anything under /click/tests/. Do NOT add new features beyond making the missing-stream case not crash.
- Verify with a throwaway script OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/check_streams.py) that monkeypatches `sys.stdout`, `sys.stderr` (and `sys.stdin`) to `None` and checks that `click.echo('hi')`, `click.echo('hi', err=True)`, `click.echo(b'hi')`, `click.echo()` (no message), `click.secho('hi', fg='red')`, a `click.progressbar(range(3))` context manager, and `click.echo_via_pager(['a'])` all run without raising, and that `click.echo('hi')` with a normal stdout still prints normally. Also confirm `click.utils._default_text_stdout()` returns None when `sys.stdout is None`.
- Then run the full pre-existing test suite again and compare with the baseline: no pre-existing green test may fail (pay special attention to tests/test_utils.py, tests/test_termui.py, tests/test_basic.py).

Report back: exact root cause, the diff applied (files + lines), commands run, baseline failures, final pass/fail counts, and the output of your throwaway verification script.

BUG REPORT (from the user): "There is a bug in `src/click/decorators.py`. Once it is fixed, the test `tests.test_arguments::test_when_argument_decorator_is_used_multiple_times_cls_is_preserved` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

Expected behaviour (from the test name): when a user creates a reusable `@click.argument(...)` decorator (e.g. `def deco(f): return click.argument('x', cls=MyArgument)(f)`) or applies the same decorator object to several functions, the `cls=` passed to `click.argument` must be preserved on every application. Today `argument()`'s inner `decorator` does `ArgumentClass = attrs.pop("cls", Argument)`, which mutates the closure's shared `attrs` dict, so on the second use `cls` is gone and the default `Argument` is used instead. Compare with `option()` in the same file, which already copies attrs first ("Issue 926, copy attrs, so pre-defined options can re-use the same cls=").

Your job: fix this in /click/src/click/decorators.py, minimally and in the same style as the existing `option()` fix (copy the attrs dict inside the inner decorator before popping `cls`). Do NOT edit or delete anything under /click/tests/. Do not add features.

Requirements:
- FIRST run the pre-existing test suite and record the baseline failures: `cd /click && python -m pytest tests -q` (if `click` is not importable, `pip install -e .` first).
- Apply the minimal fix.
- Verify with a throwaway script OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/check_argument_cls.py) that: (a) a single `click.argument('x', cls=CustomArg)` application still uses CustomArg; (b) the SAME decorator object applied to two different functions uses CustomArg both times; (c) a reusable decorator factory applied twice preserves cls; (d) `click.option` still behaves the same; (e) normal arguments still work end-to-end through a CliRunner command.
- Then run the full pre-existing test suite again and compare with the baseline: no pre-existing green test may fail (especially tests/test_arguments.py, tests/test_options.py, tests/test_basic.py, tests/test_commands.py).

Report back: exact root cause, the diff applied (file + lines), commands run, baseline failures, final pass/fail counts, and the output of your throwaway verification script.

BUG REPORT (from the user): "There is a bug in `src/click/core.py`. Once it is fixed, the test `tests.test_options::test_missing_required_flag` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

Expected behaviour (from the test name and from click's documented behaviour): a required flag option, e.g.

    @click.command()
    @click.option('--foo', is_flag=True, required=True)
    def cli(foo): ...

invoked with no arguments must fail with exit code 2 and an error like "Error: Missing option '--foo'." (i.e. a MissingParameter error), instead of silently passing with foo=False. Look at `Option.__init__` in /click/src/click/core.py (around the `is_flag`/`default` handling) and at `Parameter.process_value` / `value_is_missing` and `Option.consume_value`; the root cause is likely that a required bool flag is given a default of False, so the missing-value check never fires. Fix it in the source (do NOT edit any test file).

Requirements:
- Run the pre-existing test suite FIRST and record which tests fail before your change: `cd /click && python -m pytest tests -x -q` (or without -x) using the installed/dev environment (try `python -m pytest`; if click isn't importable, `pip install -e .` first). Record the baseline failures.
- Make the minimal fix in /click/src/click/core.py. Do not make out-of-scope changes, do not add features, do not modify or delete any file under /click/tests/.
- Verify: write a temporary throwaway script OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/check.py) that exercises the expected behaviour with click.testing.CliRunner (required flag missing -> exit code 2, 'Missing option' in output; flag given -> works; non-required flag -> default False still works; `--foo` with is_flag + required + default=True still works), and run the full pre-existing test suite again to confirm no pre-existing green test broke (compare against your baseline).
- Also check related behaviours that could regress: `click.option('--foo', is_flag=True, required=True, default=False)`, `multiple=True` flags, `flag_value`, `prompt=True` flags, and `tests/test_termui.py` prompt tests.

Report back: the exact root cause, the diff you applied (file + lines), the commands you ran, the baseline failing tests, and the final test results (pass/fail counts) plus the output of your throwaway verification script.

BUG REPORT (from the user): "There is a bug in `src/click/types.py`. Once it is fixed, the test `tests.test_types::test_symlink_resolution` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

Expected behaviour: `click.Path(resolve_path=True)` must fully resolve the path, i.e. make it absolute AND resolve symlinks (see the docstring of `Path` in src/click/types.py, around lines 760-764: "if this is true, then the path is fully resolved before the value is passed onwards. This means that it's absolute and symlinks are resolved.").

Likely root cause to verify: in `Path.convert` (src/click/types.py, around lines 837-843) the code does

    if self.resolve_path:
        # realpath on Windows Python < 3.8 doesn't resolve symlinks
        if os.path.islink(rv):
            rv = os.readlink(rv)
        rv = os.path.realpath(rv)

`os.readlink()` returns the raw link target, which for a *relative* symlink (e.g. `ln -s target link` inside a directory) is a path relative to the link's own directory, not to the current working directory. Feeding that into `os.path.realpath` therefore resolves it against the wrong base directory and produces a wrong (or non-absolute-looking) result. `os.path.realpath` already resolves symlinks correctly on POSIX, so the readlink step is both unnecessary and harmful there; it was only a workaround for Windows Python < 3.8. Determine the correct minimal fix yourself (e.g. use `pathlib.Path(rv).resolve()` for the general case, or restrict the readlink workaround to Windows < 3.8) and make sure it still handles `path_type=bytes`/`str`/`pathlib.Path` and `allow_dash` correctly, and that `exists`/`file_okay`/`dir_okay` checks still work.

Requirements:
- FIRST run the pre-existing test suite and record baseline failures: `cd /click && python -m pytest tests -q` (if `click` is not importable, `pip install -e .` first).
- Do NOT edit or delete anything under /click/tests/. Do not add features; only fix the divergence from the documented behaviour.
- Write a throwaway verification script OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/check_symlink.py) using tempfile/tmp_path-like setup that checks: (a) an absolute symlink to a file resolves to the real file; (b) a RELATIVE symlink (created with os.symlink with a relative target, e.g. os.symlink('real.txt', 'link.txt') inside a temp dir) resolves to the absolute real path of the target; (c) a symlink to a directory; (d) a chain of two symlinks; (e) a plain non-symlink path still becomes absolute; (f) `resolve_path=True` with `path_type=pathlib.Path` and with bytes still works; (g) `Path(exists=True, resolve_path=True)` still fails properly for a missing path. Run the script from a directory that is NOT the directory containing the symlink, so a wrong relative resolution is actually detected.
- Then run the full pre-existing test suite again and compare with the baseline: no pre-existing green test may fail (especially tests/test_types.py, tests/test_arguments.py, tests/test_options.py, tests/test_basic.py).

Report back: exact root cause, the diff applied (file + lines), commands run, baseline failures, final pass/fail counts, and the output of your throwaway verification script.

BUG REPORT (from the user): "There is a bug in `src/click/core.py`. Once it is fixed, the test `tests.test_arguments::test_envvar_flag_value` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

So: the bug is in /click/src/click/core.py and concerns the interaction of an option's `flag_value` with an environment variable (`envvar`). The hidden test is named `test_envvar_flag_value` and lives in tests/test_arguments.py. Work out the exact expected behaviour from the repository itself (docs/options.rst section about `flag_value`/`is_flag=False`, docs/arguments.rst, CHANGES.rst, existing tests in tests/test_arguments.py and tests/test_options.py such as test_type_from_flag_value, test_show_default_boolean_flag_value, test_nargs_envvar, test_empty_envvar), then find the divergence in src/click/core.py and fix it minimally.

Hints to investigate (verify each yourself, do not trust blindly):
- `Option.__init__` around lines 2504-2535 (is_flag / flag_value / type guessing / `_flag_needs_value`).
- `Option.get_default` (around line 2783) for non-bool flags.
- `Parameter.consume_value` (around line 2239) and `Option.consume_value` (around line 2857): the order of command line / envvar / default_map / default, and what happens when a flag option gets its value from the environment.
- `Option.value_from_envvar` / `Parameter.value_from_envvar`.
- Note the 8.0.1 changelog entry: "Flag options guess their type from ``flag_value`` if given, like regular options do from ``default``." Consider whether an option with `is_flag=True, flag_value=..., envvar=...` or `is_flag=False, flag_value=..., envvar=...` behaves as documented.

BUG REPORT (from the user): "There is a bug in `src/click/core.py`. Once it is fixed, the test `tests.test_defaults::test_flag_default_map` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

So the bug is in /click/src/click/core.py and concerns a *flag* option whose value comes from `Context.default_map` (see docs/commands.rst section about `default_map`, docs/options.rst, and the existing tests tests/test_defaults.py, tests/test_commands.py::test_default_maps, tests/test_options.py::test_show_default_default_map, tests/test_context.py::test_parameter_source). The hidden test lives in tests/test_defaults.py and is named `test_flag_default_map`.

Investigate these places in src/click/core.py (verify each yourself, don't trust blindly):
- `Option.get_default` (around line 2783) — for `is_flag and not is_bool_flag` it ignores `ctx.default_map` entirely and instead scans `ctx.command.params` for a param with the same name and a truthy `default`, returning that param's `flag_value`. Consider what happens when the user supplies the value via `default_map` instead (e.g. a pair of `--upper/--lower` style flags with `flag_value=` and `default=True` on one of them, invoked with `default_map={'name': 'lower'}`): the default_map value should win, as `Parameter.get_default` documents ("Looks at ``ctx.default_map`` first", and `Context.lookup_default`).
- `Parameter.get_default` (around line 2190) and `Parameter.consume_value` (around line 2239) / `Option.consume_value` (around line 2857): the order command line -> envvar -> default_map -> default, and the `ParameterSource` reported.
- Also check how `show_default` renders for such flags (tests/test_options.py::test_show_default_boolean_flag_value) and make sure that keeps working.
